newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seeks talks with U.S. telecom firms on rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila seeks talks with U.S. telecom firms on rates.

text.p: Philippine telecommunication firms and the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) are asking the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to allow negotiations between carriers to determine a reduction in international call rates.

In an industry position paper released on Monday, the country's nine international gateway facility (IGF) operators and the NTC recommended that "carriers should be left alone to commercially negotiate" the reduction in accounting rates.
Accounting rates refer to the cost of international calls, now at $1.00 per minute between the United States and the Philippines, which is split into half by the carriers that facilitate the call.

Last December, the FCC announced a proposed across-the-board rate reduction. For upper-middle and middle income countries under which the Philippines is classified, the FCC proposed that the accounting rate be reduced to 38 cents a minute within two years.

"It definitely needs a longer transition, other than the two years ...," the industry paper said. The telecom firms pointed out that the Philippines' bid to improve local telecommunications networks may be hindered by the revenue losses which will result from an abrupt reduction in rates.
Local calls are largely subsidised by revenues from international calls.

The position paper was drafted by the NTC in consultation with IGF operators including Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc, Globe Telecom GMCR Inc, Philippine Telegraph and Telephone Corp and Smart Communications Co Inc, a unit of Metro Pacific Corp.
Other companies involved were ICC Telecoms, Philippine Global Communications, Eastern Telecommunications Phils Inc and Isla Communications Co Inc.
